lessons: Respect big early-season line moves. review.units_text: - Straight up: 7-5. ATS: no picks (0-0). Totals: 1-0 (NYK-BOS Under). Small value: 2-1 (ATL ML W, NOP ML L, Under W) plus MEM ML lean W. About +1.5u at preview prices (ATL +0.77, Under +0.90, MEM +0.80 on 0.5u, NOP -1), before fees.
day_summary: Straight up: 7-5. ATS: no picks (0-0). Totals: 1-0 (NYK-BOS Under). Small value: 2-1 (ATL ML W, NOP ML L, Under W) plus MEM ML lean W. About +1.5u at preview prices (ATL +0.77, Under +0.90, MEM +0.80 on 0.5u, NOP -1), before fees.
Passed spreads in hindsight: dogs I skipped under L4 went 3-1 ATS (LAC, MEM, SAC covered; WSH didn't). Favorites overall went roughly 4-8 ATS tonight, reversing the 9-2 opening run.
Totals in hindsight: 7 of 12 went Under the close, and 9 of the last 14 games (two nights) did.
lessons: Don't build a rule off one day's trend. The "5+ points of edge for dogs" bar came from one 9-2 favorites night; tonight dogs covered and it cost me three winners where my own margin was right (LAC, MEM, SAC). Revert to ~3.5-4 points of edge, sized small.
Don't extrapolate a team's opener in either direction. CHI (lost by 43, then won), DAL (bad defense, then won by 16), IND and SAC all reversed. Weight one game lightly.
When a key player is questionable, also ask what wins the game if he plays. I trimmed SAS for Fox, he played, and the real issue (HOU's size and free throws) went unweighed.

lessons.title: Trust my own judgement; markets are an input, not the answer.
lessons.body: (User directive 2026-10-21.) Don't flip a pick just because the line moved. But when I can name the reason for a sharp move (a real roster hole like no center, or a key returnee confirmed), move my own number by that amount; don't just keep the pick at lower confidence. Only when I can't find a reason do I keep the pick at slightly lower confidence, and then don't bet it: when ML money runs far ahead of tickets against me (2026-10-29: 68% money / 38% tickets on MIA) and I can't name why, keep the pick, skip the value bet. That rule is 2-for-2 (2026-10-30: passed CLE as the line moved to ATL against CLE tickets; ATL won). (2026-10-22: UTA with no center vs Edey lost by 20; SAC-LAC lost by 25. 2026-10-26: moved to DET on Embiid's rest and to IND on BKN's B2B; both won by 13+. lessons.title: A total's line move is an input, not an automatic pass.
lessons.body: When the move goes against my lean, re-check my named reasons (pace, shooting, rest, first games); if they hold, take the lean at the better moved number, smaller size. Record of following the move: 5-4 (2026-10-29: CHA-DET Under won by 27.5, ORL-TOR Under lost by 4.5; 2026-10-28: POR-LAL Under lost by 31.5, built on POR's two-game defense vs PHX/SAC; don't bet a total when my reasons are tiny samples against weak opponents; BOS-DET and CHA-BKN moves were right; 2026-10-26 Unders in ORL-NYK and TOR-MIN won by 11.5 and 20.5 after totals fell against 87-92% Over tickets; 2026-10-23 both totals rose 4-5 points and went Under by 17.5 and 56.5, and I passed on a stated Under lean in CLE-PHI). Two first-week games on 2026-10-23 landed far below the line; don't assume shootouts in openers.

lessons.title: Dogs with points: need real edge, but don't build rules off one night.
lessons.body: My dogs-with-points are 2-4, so require ~3.5-4 points of edge on my own margin (not 5+) and size small. The 5+ bar came from one 9-2 favorites night (2026-10-22) and cost three winners on 2026-10-24 (LAC, MEM, SAC covered; favorites went 4-8 ATS). 2026-10-26: passed LAC +15.5 (2.5 pts edge) covered by 8.5, BKN +7.5 lost by 27; when a dog misses the bar, it's my margin that needs work, not the bar. Still respect a clearly better, healthier roster and a team's first real game.

lessons.title: Achilles/ACL returnees: no night-one penalty by default.
lessons.body: Tatum went 6-23 in game one, then 36 in game two; Haliburton, Lillard, Kyrie and VanVleet have been fine. Judge each on preseason form and minutes.

lessons.title: Weight a single game lightly, in both directions, but by game three treat it as a trend.
lessons.body: CHI, DAL, IND and SAC reversed their openers on 2026-10-24; CHA bounced back from 81 points to beat MIA on 2026-10-25. But CHI's 23% three-point shooting over three games was real (lost to WSH 2026-10-25), and I called NYK's 0-2 cold offense noise, then it lost at home to a Banchero-less ORL (9-38 from three, 2026-10-26). A trend only counts for the same roster, and a named trend must move my number: GSW's 0-3 included a game without Curry/Draymond/Podziemski and it won by 20 at DEN once they returned; I called MIA's offense a trend but still had MIA 62%, and it lost to DAL (2026-10-27). But a shooting slump by a proven, unchanged core gets half weight: I priced NYK's 0-3 (Brunson/Bridges cold) as a trend and NYK beat DET by 14 with a 37-13 third (2026-10-28). Full weight is for structural problems (no center, turnovers, a missing creator). Strip a single blowout from early net ratings before pricing: POR's +18 net was mostly a 41-point opener and healthy, rested MEM won there by 21 (Grizzlies ML hit, 2026-10-30). Same for totals: an Under resting partly on a team's shooting slump is half an Under (TOR scored 129 off a slump, 2026-10-29); turnover trends held (LAC 24, CHA 23, ORL 20).

lessons.title: For a questionable star, also ask what decides the game if he plays, and write conditional plays with a clear trigger and price limit.
lessons.body: Trimmed SAS for Fox; he played, and HOU's size and free throws (28-31) won it. Conditionals are 2-0 (2026-10-27: DAL +7.5 with Flagg active, won outright; MIL ML with Nembhard out); untriggered ones aren't counted (2026-10-29: PHI -5.5 would have lost, DAL ML would have won).
